text.en:
1. (1) This Act may be cited as the Passports Act, 1966,
and shall come into force on such date as the Minister may
by notification in the Gazette appoint, such date not being
earlier than the date on which the notification is published.

(2) This Act shall apply throughout the Federation.

2. (1) Every person entering the Federation from any place
beyond the Federation shall} produce to an immigration
officer a passport; and such passport shall, in the case of
an alien, have a valid visa for the Federation issued on the
authority of and by or on behalf of the Government of
the Federation.

(2) Every person leaving the Federation for a place
beyond the Federation shall,| if required so to do by an
immigration officer produce to that officer a passport.

(3) An immigration officer may, in relation to any pass-
port produced under this section, put to any person
producing such passport such questions as he thinks
necessary; and such person shall answer any such question
truthfully.

(4) An immigration officer may make on any passport
produced under this section such endorsement as he thinks
fit.

3. The provisions of section 2 shall apply to a person
entering or leaving the States of Malaya or a Borneo State
from or to any part of the Federation, as they apply to a
person entering or leaving the Federation from or to any
place beyond the Federation, as if—

(a) references therein to the Federation were construed
as references to States of Malaya or the Borneo
State, as the case may be; and

(b) references to a passport were construed as including
an internal travel document issued under any
written law relating to immigration for the time
being in force in the Federation.

4. The Minister may by order exempt any person or class
of persons from the provisions of section 2 or section 3 or
both; and such exemption may be subject to such conditions
as he may direct and may be permanent or for a limited
period.

5. (1) Without prejudice t

liable, upon an order in that behalf being made by the

Provided that no such order shall apply to a citizen of
the Federation.

(2) An order made by the Controller under sub-section
(1), may provide for the detention in custody, for such
period as may be necessary for the purpose of making
arrangements for his removal, of the person to whom the
order applies; and such person may pursuant to the order
be detained either in a prison or in any other place
appointed by the Controller for that purpose.

(3) Any person to whom an order under sub-section (1)
applies may be conducted across the frontier or placed on
board a suitable vessel by an immigration officer, police
officer or officer of customs, and may be lawfully detained
on board such vessel during the period that such vessel is
within the Federation or the territorial waters thereof.

6. (1) Where an order made under sub-section (1) of
section 5 applies to a person who was brought into the
Federation in a vessel, the master of the vessel and the
master of any other vessel belonging to the same owner
shall, if required by the/ Controller and subject to sub-
section (2), receive such|person on board his vessel and

(2) A requirement mentioned under sub-section (1) shall
have no effect unless it 1s made within twelve months of

(3) The master of a vessel |failing to comply with the
provisions of sub-section (1) shall be liable on conviction
to imprisonment for a term not excccding six months or to
a fine not exceeding one thousand dollars or to both such
imprisonment and fine.

7. The master and the owners and agents of any vessel
from which any person enters| the Federation contrary to
the provisions of this Act shall be jointly and severally
liable for all expenses incurred by the Government in
detaining and maintaining such|person pending deportation;
and such expenses shall be recoverable as a debt due to the
Government from the master, owners and agents.

8. The master of a vessel may use all reasonable and proper
means (including force if necessary) to prevent any person
from entering the Federation contrary to the provisions of
this Act.

9. If any question arises in any [proceedings under this Act,
or with reference to anything done or proposed to be done
under this Act, as to whether a) person—

(a) is an alien or not; or

(b) belongs to any particular class of persons exempted
from any of the provisions of this Act,

the onus of proving that the nelson is not an alien or that
he belongs to such class, as the case may be, shall lie upon
that person.

10. Any person who enters of attempts to enter or is
reasonably suspected of having |entered the Federation in
contravention of the provisions of this Act may be arrested
without warrant by any immigration officer, police officer
or officer of customs.

11. The Minister may make [regulations generally for
carrying out the purposes of this Act.

Offences. 12, (1) Any person who—

(a) forges, alters or tampers with any passport or
internal travel document, or any visa or endorse-
ment thereon, or without lawful authority uses
or attempts to use, or has in his possession, any
passport or internal travel document which has
been so forged, altered or tampered with;

(b) makes any false document intending to use such
document as a passport for the purpose of this
Act, or uses such document for that purpose;

(c) personates or falsely} represents himself to be or
not to be a person to whom a passport or internal
travel document, has been duly issued;

(d) with intent to obtain for himself or any other person
a passport, internal travel document, or an
endorsement or visa on a passport, knowingly
makes any false statement or produces any docu-
ment which is to|his knowledge false in any
particular;

(e) without lawful authority, has in his possession any
passport or internal travel document which has
been obtained as a result of making any material
statement which was false or misleading, or as a
result of the production of false evidence;

(f) allows any person to have possession of any pass-
port issued for his use alone, intending or
knowing that such [passport may be used by any
other person;

(2) without lawful. authotity, has in his possession any
passport or internal travel document issued for
the use of some person other than himself;

(4) wilfully assists any person to enter the Federation
contrary to the provisions of this Act;

(i) wilfully assists any person to contravene any of
the provisions of this Act;

(j) obstructs or hinders any immigration officer, police
officer or officer of customs in the discharge of
his duty under this Act; or

(k) attempts to commit or abets the commission of any
offence under this Act,

"Commonwealth citizen" means a person who is a

"entry" and "enter" means entry and to enter by land,
sea or air;

"immigration officer" shall have the meaning assigned
to it in the Immigration Ordinance, 1959;                   12 of 1959.

"master" includes the pilot of an aircraft;

"Minister" means the Minister charged with responsibility
for immigration;

"officer of customs" and "police officer" shall, in relation
to the States of Malaya and the States of Sabah and
Sarawak, have the meanings respectively assigned to them
in any written law relating to customs and police, in force
in the States of Malaya and the States of Sabah and
Sarawak;

"owner" in relation to a vessel includes a charterer;

"passport" means a valid passport which has been issued
to a person by or on behalf of the Government of which
he is a subject or citizen and includes any form of valid
